Configuring retries

The client retries failed requests automatically. A request is retried when the connection fails, when the server answers with status 429, or with any 5xx status. Other errors are raised immediately so that bugs in your code surface quickly.

Defaults

By default the client makes up to three attempts with exponential backoff between them. The table below lists every setting and its default value.

SettingDefaultMeaning
max_attempts3Total attempts including the first one
backoff0.5Initial delay in seconds, doubled after each failure
max_backoff30Upper bound for a single delay in seconds

Custom policies

Pass a RetryPolicy when you create the client to change how failures are handled. The policy applies to every request made through that client instance.

from acme import Client, RetryPolicy

client = Client(retry=RetryPolicy(max_attempts=5, backoff=1.0))

import { Client, RetryPolicy } from "acme";

const client = new Client({ retry: new RetryPolicy({ maxAttempts: 5, backoff: 1.0 }) });

Warning

Retrying requests that are not idempotent, such as payments, can perform the same operation twice. Disable retries for those calls or send an idempotency key with every request.

Per-request overrides

Any single call can override the client policy with the retry argument. Passing retry=None disables retries for that call only, which is the recommended setting for non-idempotent operations.

client.charge(amount=1000, retry=None)

Retries are logged at the debug level, including the attempt number and the delay before the next attempt, so you can verify the policy in your own logs.
